intelligence.essence: The Agreement fix-3 eye proved every remedy by real tap at both widths — the alias survives, the certificate name paints, the door holds until Continue, the unfold walks 1→37, the deck and the letter walk 1→37 and land on the bridge — and then it sent the round BACK. Not because anything failed to work, but because at phone width the page does not read: the certificate title is hidden behind the hero name, the door heading loses its first and last letters behind the corner jewels, the "already claimed" banner's first line is clipped at both edges, and the final board's title runs under the purple diamond orb. The function is proven; the presentation is not. A round whose remedies all pass can still go back — on the reading alone. Proven by tap is not proven to the eye.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you built a beautiful toy, sweetheart — every button works, every wheel turns, it does everything it is supposed to do! But when you hold it up to show your friend, the pretty picture on the front is covered up by a sticker — so your friend can't see what it says! The toy works perfectly, sweetheart — but the showing part is broken. So we check both: does it work, AND can you read it?
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like this, love — you bake the most wonderful cake, dear, every layer perfect, and then you put the lid on crooked so nobody can see the writing on top. The cake is delicious, love — but the message is hidden! So we taste it AND we look at it, dear — the work is only done when it reads as beautifully as it works.
